raw_response:
I am still going to keep most of my land in the wheat-maize rotation, because that is what I know best and it gives the family steadier income. Cotton can make money in a good year, but it ties up the land longer and needs more picking labor, so I will only keep some cotton on a smaller piece. I have farmed here a long time, and with well water available I do not want to take too much risk. The extension people talk about cutting fertilizer to the exact rate, but on my land I usually keep it a bit safe, especially for wheat. Input prices are not low now, so I will not push too hard. I will use improved seed where it matters, split fertilizer on wheat and maize, and irrigate when the crop stage really needs it. Since some people in my family work off-farm, I also need the plan to fit the labor we actually have at home.

For wheat, I will keep the better, flatter land in the rotation and sow in early October after simple land preparation. I usually put base fertilizer before sowing, then topdress once around jointing, because one-time application is easy but not as reliable. Wheat is where I do not want to save too much, because if it gets weak over winter or turns yellow in spring, yield drops fast. After harvest in June, I will plant summer maize right away on the same land. The gap is very short, so I will not do heavy tillage, just a quick turnaround and sow as soon as possible if there is moisture. For cotton, I will keep a smaller area. Cotton needs more watching and more hand labor, but it spreads risk. If grain prices are only ordinary this year, cotton still gives me another chance for cash.
